summary: Two checks built, both proven red on planted defects and red on real historical trees, and the handed-off derive oracle table verified assertion by assertion. O13 (tests/test_ownership.py) opens every path/file.py::symbol citation in src/ AND docs/ -- 523 of them -- resolving the cited path exactly rather than by basename, requiring the FULL dotted symbol, and, where a sentence is attributed in as many words, looking for that sentence inside the cited symbol. It FAILS on the tree as it stands, once, on a citation in a file I do not own: src/eval/api.py:75 cites tests/test_couplings.py::C2 and that file defines no C2 (the check is check_c2_escapes_refused at tests/test_couplings.py:283); the exact find/replace is in unfinished. K15 (tests/test_contract.py) reads all 109 Gate constructions and settles the four claims a reason makes that the source text alone can settle; it is GREEN on the tree and FAILS on e4c5e4b, 7e902ba and 694f156 on the real shape-(b) instance those commits carried. THE BRIEF IS REFUTED TWICE, both times with measurements. (1) 'the existence half alone would have caught 23 of the 25 false citations': it would have caught NONE. a2ffc08's own commit message says twenty-three of the twenty-five NAMED A SYMBOL THAT EXISTS, and running the finished O13 against 2e8a63e -- the commit before that repair -- reports exactly what it reports today, one finding and no quotation findings. (2) 'shape (b) is the most mechanisable': the broad keyword scan ('cannot', 'never', 'no ... can', 'unreachable') was run over 25 commits and reported THE SAME FOUR SITES at every one of them, all four correct prose, and zero true instances -- because the true instances were reachable=<expression>, which no static reader can evaluate. What shipped instead is a closed list of self-referential phrases, calibrated over the same 25 commits: it fires on exactly the three that carried the defect and on nothing else. The derive oracle table in .rework/audits/x_spine.json is CORRECT: all 86 of its assertions were executed against the live functions and none had a wrong expectation; I applied it to a scratch copy of tests/test_derive.py, ran it (575 oracle cases, smoke OK) and then broke one derive guard to prove the block is load-bearing. Four assertions are ADDED to it for edges it did not reach. Suite: contract 15+54 green, census 7 green, assemble 9 green, couplings 4 green, derive 575/0; ownership 13+27 with O13's one finding, which is the dispatch.

findings.detail: O13 -- 'citations open: the cited file contains the cited symbol'. It goes past O12 in four concrete ways, each of which was a way for a citation to be checkable-and-unchecked. (a) IT SCANS docs/. O12's population is `mods`, i.e. src/**/*.py; docs/03_WIRING.md and docs/04_CONTRACT.md carry citations O12 has never opened. (b) IT RESOLVES THE PATH EXACTLY -- an exact match on the tail of a repository-relative path -- where O12 resolves by BASENAME, so `spine/derive.py::x` can no longer be satisfied by some other derive.py. (c) IT REQUIRES THE FULL DOTTED SYMBOL, where O12 accepts `Config.owned_bye` on a file that declares `Config` and no `owned_bye` (self-test case 'a dotted citation whose HEAD resolves and whose TAIL does not' asserts O12 green and O13 red on one tree). (d) IT OPENS tests/ as a citation TARGET, which is where the tree's one live false citation is. THE QUOTATION HALF: a citation followed, with nothing between it but an attribution verb from a closed list, by a double-quoted span of >=4 words carrying no code punctuation, is a claim the cited symbol CONTAINS that span; the span is looked for in that symbol's own source, compared after casefolding and flattening punctuation, and the finding names the SIBLING SYMBOL that does carry it when one does. Every narrowing has a measured reason, and they are in the check's own CANNOT CATCH block: single quotes are excluded because this tree's prose is full of possessives and matching them reported 27 sites of which 24 were `build's`, `forward's`, `draw_stream's`; code-punctuation spans are excluded because assemble.COUPLINGS' rows are written over five lines with other arguments interleaved, so a CORRECT citation of one fails a substring test (two of the three sites the first version flagged were exactly that); and the verb list is closed because 'A for B's <quote>' -- the shape twelve of the twenty citations corrected in spine/compose.py on 2026-09-04 actually had -- must ABSTAIN rather than guess. On the current tree it reports: 523 citations opened against 56 indexed files, 3 quotation pairs checked, 3 into the frozen old tree or outside the rebuild left alone (compare.py::main twice, verification.py::Reconstructor.__init__ once), and 4 naming a function-local ADMITTED AND COUNTED.

Whole-tree plant, on a scratch copy outside the repo (git archive HEAD into /tmp/.../plant): inserted `spine/units.py::Clock.cnovert` into src/spine/derive.py, `spine/lever.py::Lever.env_name_four` into docs/03_WIRING.md, and changed the quoted sentence in src/data/api.py's DATALevers citation to one levers.py does not contain -> O13 reports all three, including the docs/ one and the quotation one. Historical: same check against 2e8a63e (a2ffc08^, before the 25-citation repair) reports one finding and zero quotation findings, identical to today.

findings.detail: K15 -- 'a Gate's reason names a lever that exists, a value it can hold, and no impossibility on a reachable gate'. Four rules over all 109 Gate constructions in src/ (spine/gate.py excluded as the record's own declaration). RULE 1, the name: every PREFIX_NAME= a reason spells must be a declared lever env name, generated as PREFIX_FIELD by spine/lever.py::Lever.env_name_for -- an operator sent to a knob that does not exist has been sent nowhere. RULE 2, the value: a literal spelled beside that name is coerced by a MIRROR of spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce and must survive it and be inside the lever's declared `choices`. Mirroring coerce rather than hand-rolling the type test is not tidiness -- the hand-rolled first version reported OPT_LR_RESTARTS='off' as a value that lever cannot hold, three times, in three correct gates, because coerce's bool branch reads 'off' as False. RULE 3, the rendered value: `PREFIX_NAME={expr}` in an f-string is traced back through the enclosing function's assignments (tuple unpacking included -- without it FAB_BALANCE={balance_w} reported false, because fabric/api.py binds it in a three-way unpack) and must reach a read of that lever's own field or its d_ wire spelling; it ABSTAINS when the trace reaches a parameter, which is 2 of the tree's 48 rendered values. RULE 4, shape (b): a reason may not assert impossibility on a Gate the source declares reachable, using a CLOSED list of self-referential phrases. Live report: 109 gates, 89 lever names, 18 literal values constrained, 48 rendered, 2 abstained, 15 gates whose reachability is computed and whose reasons rule 4 therefore cannot judge. Two things it refuses to check and says so: the arithmetic inside a reason ('16 backward // 4 vs 10' is four runtime quantities), and `value=`/`threshold=`, which are rendered from derived quantities on purpose (`f"balance={balance_w} x warm={round(bal_scale, 4)}"`), so extending rule 3 to them would fire on correct gates.
findings.repro: cd /home/user/LLM-Test && python3 tests/test_contract.py   # 15 checks + 54 self-test cases, 0 failing; 8 new K15 cases, 5 red and 3 admit (correct-gate-with-negation, rendered-from-parameter, and the identical impossibility reason on the reachable=False arm). Whole-tree plants on scratch copies: CAP_TARGETS -> CAP_TARGET (rule 1 red), OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 -> =lots (rule 2 type, red), DATA_SOURCE=synthetic -> =corpuz at src/data/api.py:491 (rule 2 choices, red), f"DATA_CORPUS_CAP={int(dat.corpus_cap)}" -> {int(dat.val_cap)} (rule 3, red). Rule 4 needed no plant: the finished check run against the real trees at e4c5e4b, 7e902ba and 694f156 reports "src/opt/api.py:1013 Gate 'opt.lr.sched' is built reachable and its reason says 'structurally unreachable'" and passes at 6d8eb0e and after, where it was fixed.

findings.detail: THE ONE LIVE O13 FINDING, and it is in a file I do not own. src/eval/api.py:75 reads 'tests/test_couplings.py::C2 is what holds it'. tests/test_couplings.py defines no symbol C2: C2 is the REPORT TAG that check_c2_escapes_refused (tests/test_couplings.py:283) prints through _report. Fourteen of the fifteen citations from src/ into tests/ name a real function (check_o11_no_unnamed_clock_arithmetic, check_o12_citations_name_symbols, check_o9_one_config_per_signature, k13_live_counts, stub_reads, api_signatures, _split_items), so this is the outlier against the tree's own convention rather than a second convention. The RULING it supports is unaffected -- check_c2_escapes_refused really is what holds 'a compute may not reach past its declared sources' -- only the pointer is wrong. Exact find/replace in unfinished. Until it lands, tests/test_ownership.py reports 13 checks with 1 failing.

THE BRIEF'S CLAIM THAT AN EXISTENCE CHECK 'ALONE WOULD HAVE CAUGHT 23 OF THE 25 FALSE CITATIONS' IS BACKWARDS, and the tree says so itself. a2ffc08's commit message: 'Reading both spine tables end to end found TWENTY-FIVE false ones -- twenty-three naming a symbol that EXISTS and is the WRONG ONE, which is the exact hole O12's own docstring says it cannot reach, and two attributing a sentence the cited file no longer contains.' The diff confirms it: ckpt/api.py::install_save_signal -> ::resume_source, sig/api.py::warm_up -> ::state_dict, data/api.py::open_areas -> ::draw_stream, fabric/api.py::build -> ::forward -- in every pair BOTH symbols exist. MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED: the finished O13 was run against 2e8a63e (a2ffc08^), the tree carrying all twenty-five, and reported one existence finding (the same tests/test_couplings.py::C2 it reports today) and zero quotation findings. O13 catches none of that sweep, and its own docstring says so in its first paragraph rather than in a footnote. What it does close is the mechanical residue: docs/ was never opened at all, and a dotted tail was never resolved.

findings.detail: SHAPE (b) IS NOT 'THE MOST MECHANISABLE' IN THE BROAD FORM THE BRIEF DESCRIBES, and implementing it as described would have shipped a check that cries wolf four times and catches nothing. The broad rule -- scan a statically-reachable Gate's reason for 'cannot', 'never', 'no ... can', 'unreachable' -- was run over the trees of 25 commits (8cb00e3..1e8cc54). It reported THE SAME FOUR SITES at every commit and all four are correct prose: data/api.py's redraw gate explaining why epoch 0 reads 'armed-and-did-not-fire rather than unreachable'; opt/api.py saying a counter is 'rendered here, never computed here'; capacity/api.py:413 arguing the state is 'an UNMET CONDITION and not an unreachable one'; capacity/api.py:601 saying 'no lift can have happened yet' about lifts and not about its own gate. It caught ZERO true instances in 25 commits, because the true ones are reachable=<expression> (opt.lr.min_frac's `reachable=sched_live and min_frac > 0.0`) and a static reader cannot evaluate those. Two other tempting rules were tried and dropped the same way: matching the reserved capitalised word UNREACHABLE fires on fabric/api.py:570, which correctly says 'every gate below this one reports UNREACHABLE'. WHAT SHIPPED, AND ITS CALIBRATION: a closed list of phrases that can only be about the gate carrying them ('structurally unreachable', 'cannot fire', 'cannot be met', 'no configuration can', ...). Over the same 25 commits it fires on exactly three -- e4c5e4b, 7e902ba, 694f156 -- on `Gate("opt.lr.sched", sched != "none", sched, "cosine", reachable=True, reason="OPT_LR_SCHED=none: warmup, wavelength, floor, restarts, damping, envelope and re-warm are ALL structurally unreachable...")` , which is the instance opt/api.py's own repair comment describes as 'It was hard-coded True ... followed by its own reason asserting unreachability. One line making both statements.' Zero false positives across all 25.
findings.repro: for c in $(git log --format=%h | head -25); do git archive $c | tar -x -C /tmp/h/$c; cp tests/test_contract.py /tmp/h/$c/tests/; (cd /tmp/h/$c && python3 tests/test_contract.py 2>&1 | sed -n '/  K15/,/^$/p'); done   # FAIL at e4c5e4b, 7e902ba, 694f156 only

findings.detail: THE HANDED-OFF TABLE IS CORRECT: NOT ONE EXPECTATION IS WRONG. All 86 assertions in it were executed against the live spine.derive and spine.units, with an equality test that also checks the CLOCK KIND of the answer (Windows(30) and Steps(30) must not pass for one another) -- 86 passed, 0 failed. Spot-checks of the arithmetic it asserts: 52//4=13, 62//4=15, 62//64=0, 20000//16=1250, 1024//64=16, 3*10=30. The negative-Backwards loop depends on the item-1 repair in src/spine/derive.py and that repair has landed, so all 28 of its refusals hold. I then applied the block to a scratch copy of tests/test_derive.py and RAN it: 575 oracle cases, 0 mismatches, smoke OK. To prove the block is load-bearing rather than decorative I disabled one guard in the scratch derive (opt_steps_from_backwards' `isinstance(accum, Clock)`) and the run failed with "opt_steps_from_backwards accepted Windows(4) as its rate". FOUR ASSERTIONS ARE ADDED, for edges the table does not reach, each measured: opt_steps_from_backwards REFUSES accum 0 and -1 (k < 1) while accum_due CLAMPS them -- accum_due(Backwards(52), 0) and (Backwards(52), -4) are both True, by the `max(1, int(accum))` its own docstring says is deliberately untouched -- and accum_due(Backwards(-4), 4) is False. That asymmetry between two functions one screen apart is worth pinning. THREE THINGS I MEASURED AND DID NOT ADD, because each would be a new behavioural claim rather than a test of the stated one, and they are for the owner of src/spine/derive.py: every rate argument accepts a float or a string (run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), 3.0) is Windows(9) and (Epochs(3), '10') is Windows(30), because the guard is isinstance(rate, Clock) and then int()); run_windows_from_epochs has NO negative guard at the count end where opt_steps_from_backwards has one, so run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(-1), 10) is Windows(-10); and Epochs(-1) and Backwards(-1) both construct.

findings.detail: FOUND BY A WIDER VERSION OF O13'S QUOTATION RULE AND THEN EXCLUDED FROM THE SHIPPED ONE, so it is reported here instead. src/tok/levers.py:87 reads 'assemble.py::COUPLINGS declares `Coupling(src="TOK.vmax", dst="LM.d_softmax_width", compute=lambda r: int(r["TOK"].vmax))`' and goes on, in the present tense, to say 'build() will raise LeverError at startup the moment both LM and TOK are registered'. COUPLINGS declares no such row: the live row is src="LM.vocab_slots", dst="TOK.d_vocab_ceiling" (src/spine/assemble.py:850-877), and that row's own `why` says so -- 'tok/levers.py::<module> is the half that is still outstanding: its vmax paragraph reads ... present tense, of a row that has been declared here since. That correction is TOK's to make'. So this is a known-outstanding item that a check independently rediscovered, not a new one. It is NOT a K15 or O13 finding as shipped: the quoted span is a reconstruction of a multi-line Coupling call, and matching code spans by substring fires on CORRECT citations of constructions written across five lines -- which is exactly why that half of the rule was cut.
findings.repro: cd /home/user/LLM-Test && sed -n '87,96p' src/tok/levers.py && grep -n 'd_softmax_width' src/spine/assemble.py && sed -n '850,856p' src/spine/assemble.py

findings.detail: FOUR CITATIONS NAME A FUNCTION-LOCAL VARIABLE, which spine/compose.py's own header calls a defect -- 'domains/api.py::observe.dom -- a LOCAL VARIABLE, which O12's AST walk admits as a symbol because it collects Assign targets'. They are src/data/levers.py:442 and :446 (spine/derive.py::pin_tick.held and derive.py::pin_tick.held), src/spine/derive.py:730 (tok/api.py::vocab_state._), and src/spine/compose.py:250 (domains/api.py::observe.dom). O13 ADMITS all four and PRINTS the count on its report line, and this is a deliberate refusal to make it a firing rule: the fourth of them is inside the sentence that ENUMERATES the twenty corrected citations, so the rule would fire on prose whose entire subject is that the citation was wrong. A check that fires on a correct sentence is the outcome that gets a check switched off, and this repository has sixty untrippable guards on record from exactly that. The three live ones are for their files' owners; if they are repaired, the admitted count on O13's line drops from 4 to 1 and the difference is visible on every run.
findings.repro: cd /home/user/LLM-Test && python3 tests/test_ownership.py 2>&1 | grep 'naming a function-local' && sed -n '442p;446p' src/data/levers.py && sed -n '730p' src/spine/derive.py && sed -n '250p' src/spine/compose.py

unfinished.reason: tests/test_derive.py is outside my grant (tests/test_ownership.py and tests/test_contract.py only). Every assertion below was executed against the live tree, and the whole block was applied to a scratch copy and run.
unfinished.detail:
VERIFIED, NOT FORWARDED. All 86 assertions of the table in .rework/audits/x_spine.json were executed against the live spine.derive with a kind-checking equality; 86 passed, 0 had a wrong expectation. The block below is that table plus four ADDED assertions (opt_steps_from_backwards refuses accum 0 and -1; accum_due CLAMPS the same two to 1 and answers True; accum_due of a negative Backwards is False) which pin an asymmetry between two functions one screen apart. Applied to a scratch copy and run: 575 oracle cases, 0 mismatches, smoke OK. Disabling opt_steps_from_backwards' `isinstance(accum, Clock)` guard in that scratch copy makes it fail with "opt_steps_from_backwards accepted Windows(4) as its rate", so the block is load-bearing.

EDIT 1 -- the local import inside smoke(), tests/test_derive.py:119 (the string occurs once in the file):
FIND     from spine.units import Backwards, Flushes, Steps, UnitError, Windows
REPLACE  from spine.units import Backwards, Epochs, Flushes, Steps, UnitError, Windows

EDIT 2 -- insert the block below immediately after the accum_due paragraph and before the line `    # pin_tick: THE ONE FUNCTION HERE WHOSE ORACLE TABLE CANNOT SEE ITS OWN DEFECT`. The anchor to insert after (occurs once):
            derive.accum_due(bad, 4); raise AssertionError(f"non-Backwards accepted: {bad!r}")
        except UnitError:
            pass

THE BLOCK:

    # run_windows_from_epochs: EPOCHS x windows-per-epoch, the conversion compose.py::_run_windows
    # wrote inline. NO FLOOR is the property: RUN_EPOCHS=0 is refused by train/api.py with a
    # sentence and must not be clamped to one epoch here.
    assert derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), 10) == Windows(30)
    assert type(derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(1), 937)) is Windows
    assert derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(0), 10) == Windows(0)
    assert derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(1), 1) == Windows(1)
    for bad in (3, Windows(3), Steps(3), Flushes(3), Backwards(3), True, 3.0, None):
        try:
            derive.run_windows_from_epochs(bad, 10)
            raise AssertionError(f"non-Epochs accepted: {bad!r}")
        except UnitError:
            pass
    for bad in (0, -1):
        try:
            derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), bad)
            raise AssertionError(f"rate below 1 accepted: {bad!r}")
        except UnitError:
            pass

    # opt_steps_from_backwards: ONE boundary, so the divisor is accum ALONE. The two-boundary
    # divisor reports 0 due against the 15 taken on the heavy-run command -- a correct run raising
    # the P3-H29 message.
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(52), 4) == Steps(13)
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(62), 4) == Steps(15)
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(0), 4) == Steps(0)     # no floor at one
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(3), 4) == Steps(0)     # a partial step is not a step
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(1000), 1) == Steps(1000)
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(62), 64) == Steps(0)   # the two-boundary divisor
    for bad in (52, Steps(52), Windows(52), Flushes(52), Epochs(52), True, 52.0, None):
        try:
            derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(bad, 4)
            raise AssertionError(f"non-Backwards accepted: {bad!r}")
        except UnitError:
            pass
    # THE DIVISOR END OF THE SAME FUNCTION, which the handoff table did not reach: accum below one
    # is refused where accum_due CLAMPS it, and the two are deliberately different -- see the
    # accum_due assertions below.
    for bad in (0, -1):
        try:
            derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(52), bad)
            raise AssertionError(f"accum below 1 accepted: {bad!r}")
        except UnitError:
            pass
    # A NEGATIVE COUNT IS REFUSED AT EVERY MAGNITUDE. The only route is opt/api.py::counters'
    # resume subtraction, whose base is stamped FROM st.n_backward, so a negative says the backward
    # counter went BACKWARDS across a resume. Floor caught it as a side effect of rounding a partial
    # step up; truncation did not, and at accum=4 the deltas -1..-3 came back Steps(0) against a
    # `taken` of Steps(0) and counters() said nothing.
    for accum in (1, 2, 4, 8):
        for n in (-1, -2, -3, -4, -5, -8, -9):
            try:
                derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(n), accum)
                raise AssertionError(f"negative accepted: {n} at accum={accum}")
            except UnitError:
                pass

    # accum_due CLAMPS ITS RATE WHERE opt_steps_from_backwards REFUSES ONE, and that asymmetry is
    # deliberate -- accum_due's own docstring says "THE max(1, ...) BELOW IS UNTOUCHED and is still
    # the shipped read-site clamp". Pinned here so it is a decision on the record rather than a
    # difference nobody noticed.
    assert derive.accum_due(Backwards(52), 0) is True
    assert derive.accum_due(Backwards(52), -4) is True
    assert derive.accum_due(Backwards(-4), 4) is False

    # THE RATE END, ALL FIVE. units.Clock declares __int__ and __index__, so int(Windows(4)) is 4
    # and every conversion that wrote int(rate) admitted at the divisor the kind it refuses at the
    # clock: opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(52), Windows(4)) answered Steps(13).
    for fn, clk in ((derive.flush_period, Steps(20000)),
                    (derive.flush_period_windows, Windows(20000)),
                    (derive.opt_steps_from_windows, Windows(1024)),
                    (derive.opt_steps_from_backwards, Backwards(52)),
                    (derive.accum_due, Backwards(52))):
        for rate in (Windows(4), Steps(4), Flushes(4), Backwards(4), Epochs(4)):
            try:
                fn(clk, rate)
                raise AssertionError(f"{fn.__name__} accepted {rate!r} as its rate")
            except UnitError:
                pass
    try:
        derive.run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), Windows(4))
        raise AssertionError("run_windows_from_epochs accepted a Clock rate")
    except UnitError:
        pass
    # NEIGHBOURS, so the refusals above cannot be a blanket one: the bare-int rate still works.
    assert derive.flush_period(Steps(20000), 16) == Flushes(1250)
    assert derive.flush_period_windows(Windows(20000), 16) == Flushes(1250)
    assert derive.opt_steps_from_windows(Windows(1024), 64) == Steps(16)
    assert derive.accum_due(Backwards(52), 4) is True

(1) EVERY RATE ARGUMENT ACCEPTS A FLOAT OR A STRING. The guard is `isinstance(rate, Clock)` followed by `int(rate)`, so run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), 3.0) is Windows(9), run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), '10') is Windows(30), and flush_period(Steps(20000), 16.0) is Flushes(1250). If a rate is meant to be a bare integer, `isinstance(rate, Clock)` is the wrong shape of test for it. (2) NO NEGATIVE GUARD AT THE COUNT END OF run_windows_from_epochs, where opt_steps_from_backwards has one and spends a paragraph on why: run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(-1), 10) is Windows(-10). The upstream refusal is train/api.py::startup_refusals on RUN_EPOCHS, which is exactly the argument opt_steps_from_backwards' own docstring rejects for its own count end. (3) accum_due CLAMPS a rate below one where opt_steps_from_backwards REFUSES it -- accum_due(Backwards(52), 0) is True. That one is deliberate and documented in accum_due's docstring; it is listed here only so all three sit together. The block I hand over pins (3) and leaves (1) and (2) alone.
